asDecan.p: Astrologers cut each sign into three ten-degree pieces called decans, and your Sun sits in the last of Scorpio's, somewhere between twenty and twenty-nine degrees. The Golden Dawn gives that slice to Venus. Which is a bit awkward, to be honest, because Venus is in detriment in Scorpio. It's the sign opposite the one Venus rules, so the planet of pleasure and liking things has to work against the grain here, and you can usually see the effort. Scorpio is fixed water, feeling that sets hard and stays put, and Venus in it wants more than it can easily say. The first slice of the sign belongs to Mars and the Five of Cups, grief with muscle in it. The middle goes to the Sun and the Six, fond of the past. Yours is the late part, already leaning toward Sagittarius and its long views. Death is your Sun card, and the Seven is the finer grain inside it.

Your head runs a second life alongside the real one. You're sitting through a budget meeting and you've already moved to Lisbon, found the flat, picked the café on the corner. A new person texts and within an hour you've imagined the first holiday together, and possibly the way it ends. Friends ask what you want for your birthday and you honestly can't narrow it down, because six things would be lovely and each one comes with a whole story attached. I see this a lot with late Scorpio Suns. You're private, so most of this never gets said out loud. People think you're calm and a bit unreadable. Meanwhile there's a whole cinema going on behind your eyes, and on a quiet evening at home you can lose two hours to a house listing in a town you've never visited.

The less obvious gift is that you can see what a thing could become long before anyone else can. You walk into a tired rented flat with brown carpet and you've already pulled it up in your head, painted the kitchen, put a lamp in the corner where the light's bad. A friend describes a half-formed business idea over a drink, and you're the one who asks the question that makes it real, like who'd actually pay for it and how much. Venus in Scorpio doesn't want the pretty surface of anything. It wants what's underneath, what it might turn into. That makes you very good at spotting potential in people too. You'll back the quiet colleague nobody rates, and you're often right, and they remember it for years.

The harder part is that you can fall for the version of something that lives in your head and then feel oddly let down by the real one. The holiday you planned for months arrives and it's fine, genuinely nice, and you spend the second day slightly flat because it isn't the one you imagined. It happens with people as well. You meet someone, build them up in private, and then hold it against them when they turn out to be ordinary on a Tuesday. There's another thing, which is keeping options open so you never have to find out. The course you never enrol in stays perfect. The ex you never quite let go of stays perfect too. Venus in detriment wants so much that settling on one real thing can feel like losing the rest, and you know that about yourself.

When life goes wrong, a job loss, a break-up, a friend who turns on you, your first move is usually to vanish into your head. You don't make a fuss. You go quiet and start planning an escape, a move interstate, a new career, a completely different life, and for a few days that fantasy does the job of keeping you upright. About a week in, the other side shows up. You might spend money you shouldn't on something that promises a fresh start, or stay up scrolling until two, or drink a bit more than usual because it softens the edges. The people close to you often feel you've left the room without going anywhere. What helps is small and dull. Pick one real thing to fix this week, the CV, the rent, the phone call, and do only that.

What people don't always spot is how much you need a partner who'll let you want things out loud. Scorpio keeps its cards close, and Venus in detriment here often grew up feeling that its wishes were too much for other people, so you learned to want in private. The partner who works is the one who asks what you'd do with a year off and actually listens to all of it, the boat, the vineyard, the pottery studio, without laughing. You also test people, quietly, by watching whether they notice what you haven't said. That's a lot to ask of anyone. Try telling your partner one daydream a week, a small one is fine, and see what they do with it. Quite often, they'll want to come along.

You're usually at your best in work that runs on imagining something and then making someone want it. Design, property, marketing, fundraising, set and costume work, anything where you picture a finished thing and sell it before it exists. You're also good at reading what a client wants underneath what they ask for, which is Venus doing its job even in an awkward sign. The trouble comes around month three of any project. The exciting version in your head is done, the real version is all spreadsheets and emails, and three shinier projects have turned up in the meantime. You can end up with five things started and none shipped. It helps to pick one project each quarter and tell someone at work that's the one you'll finish.

At twenty this decan often lives almost entirely on possibility. You change degrees, change cities, fall hard for people who are mostly your own invention, and it can look chaotic from outside, even when inside it all feels very meaningful. By the mid-thirties most people with a late Scorpio Sun have been disappointed enough times to start testing things before falling for them. You still dream just as much, you just check the foundations first, and some of the dreams turn into an actual house, an actual business. The fifties tend to bring a kind of ease with wanting. Something of that Sagittarius lean shows up, a taste for travel and study, and you seem to enjoy the options for their own sake without needing to pick up every cup.

Keep a short list on your phone called Seven Cups. Whenever a new daydream grabs you, a move, a course, a person, a big purchase, write it down with the date. Once a month, go through the list and pick the one you'd be sorriest never to have tried. Take one small, real step toward it within the week, an email, a price, a booking. Cross off anything that's lost its pull. That's the whole practice.
